precepts.text: Unto us a child is born, and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
precepts.point: Paul confirms it: all our fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. The Corinthians Paul wrote were Israelites, for Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses' day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and the seventy elders “saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.” Sapphire is blue, and the blue flame is the hottest part of a flame. Upon the nobles he laid not his hand: “also they saw God, and did eat and drink.”

Since no man hath seen God at any time, the one they saw and ate before was Christ. Isaiah calls him God: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” The child born to us is called the mighty God and the everlasting Father. That is the God of Israel the elders saw.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

precepts.text: All our fathers were under the cloud and drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: Paul confirms it: all our fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. The Corinthians Paul wrote were Israelites, for Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses' day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Paul confirms who dealt with Israel in the wilderness: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

The Corinthians Paul wrote to were Israelites; he says “all our fathers”, and Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses’ day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High. So when the nobles of the children of Israel saw God and did eat and drink, it was Christ, the Rock that followed them, that they saw.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light; commandments and law are one and the same.
precepts.point: The Lord said, Come up to me into the mount, and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written, that thou mayest teach them. This lets you know the law and the commandments are one and the same; Christianity tries to separate the law from the commandments, but the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, lamp and light, one and the same. These are the things you build your faith on, tearing down imaginations in the minds of our people with the word of God.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

precepts.why:
The Lord told Moses, “I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.” Law and commandments together, in one gift. Proverbs shows they are one and the same: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

Lamp and light. Christianity tries to separate the law from the commandments, but the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, one and the same. These are the things you build your faith on, tearing down imaginations in the minds of our people with the word of God.

precepts.text: All the people answered with one voice, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do; Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar and twelve pillars, read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, and sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people.
precepts.point: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
“And the people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the Lord.” It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then: “all the people answered with one voice, and said, All the words which the Lord hath said will we do.” Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, built an altar under the hill and twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel, and read the book of the covenant in the audience of the people, “and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient.”

Then the blood: half in basons, half sprinkled on the altar, and “Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

Joshua was Moses' successor and did the same thing at Shechem that his predecessor did at the mountain: the people in full agreement, witnesses against themselves, “The Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey”, and a covenant made with a statute and an ordinance. We came into that covenant again, this time without the blood.

precepts.text: Moses sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people, sealing them as the purchased congregation.
precepts.point: The Most High purchased us when He instituted animal sacrifice, when Moses sprinkled the blood over the people.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
The psalmist asks the Most High to “Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed”. When did he purchase us? When he instituted animal sacrifice, when Moses sprinkled the blood over the people.

“And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basons; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar. And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

Moses sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people, sealing them as the purchased congregation. That is the congregation the psalmist is pleading for, the sheep of his pasture, Israel, asking why his anger smokes against them and that he remember Mount Zion where he dwelt.

precepts.text: Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant on the people of Israel by the twelve pillars, so only Israel was under the first covenant.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the hill, and twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel.”

He took the book of the covenant and read it to the people, “and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

The blood of the first covenant was sprinkled on the people of Israel, by twelve pillars for the twelve tribes. Only Israel was under the first covenant, and so only Israel is redeemed from its transgressions.

points: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel were called up to worship afar off, and Moses alone came near the Lord.

All the hell we catch today, we have no excuse for: it is our fault, because we agreed to do all the words the Lord had spoken. The Lord hates for us to go through it, but where he said all of this would come back on us, God is not a man that he should lie.

points: Moses told the people all the words of the Lord and all the judgments, and all the people answered with one voice: All the words which the Lord hath said will we do. That was us making a verbal agreement with the Lord; we are our ancestors back on the earth again.

points: Notice verse seven: Moses had a book of the covenant written and read it before he ever went up into the mount for the forty days. It was more than ten commandments; a whole book of what was to be done was already broken down before he went up.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

This sprinkling ties in later to the book of Hebrews and its teaching on sacrifice.
